A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GPO work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Relocated material, including the checklist and appendices, can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablation and scaling results, and a 50-participant user study in Sections 6–7 and Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds a long-trajectory BBEH experiment in Appendix E.5 and Table 4.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a long-trajectory adaptation that groups every 15 reasoning lines into one step before critical-step selection (Appendix E.5). V1 already documented short-step merging and step-count caps, but not this grouping rule. The core advantage estimation, resetting, and optimization procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds a BBEH subset representing long-context reasoning, with approximately 1,700-token prompts and 190-line reasoning chains. This extends the input conditions evaluated beyond the seven retained benchmarks; the existing user-study coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: The PPO, DPO, KTO, SimPO, and ORPO comparisons remain unchanged, including the Satori-style random-reset comparator in Figure 2. The new BBEH experiment reuses the existing base-model and DPO comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces a BBEH evaluation using 1,000 training questions, 200 test questions, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, and 15-line step grouping. The previously reported splits, evaluation metrics, and hyperparameters in Section 6 and Tables 2–3 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 8 and Appendix E.5 add a limited scalability check of whether GPO remains effective on very long trajectories with coarser step grouping. It does not isolate grouping through an ungrouped GPO control. Existing reset-selection ablations, Monte Carlo and model-size sweeps, and user-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed training averages and standard-deviation error bars in Figure 2. V2 introduces no revised run count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure; Table 4 provides no additional statistical reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports BBEH accuracy of 24.5% for the base model, 29.0% for DPO, and 36.0% for grouped GPO-DPO. These are newly reported results, not improvements over matched v1 experiments. Table 1, Figures 2–3, and user-study outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical framework, theorem statements, bounds, and Appendix C proofs are retained. New footnote 4 explains how the existing consecutive-Q advantage expression relates to Q minus V under deterministic transitions and terminal rewards; it does not substantively change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: modular critical-step optimization, online and offline theoretical support, improvements across seven benchmarks and five algorithms, and alignment with human judgments.

C2.justification: Section 8 now characterizes computational overhead as non-negligible rather than insignificant, while retaining the 1.9x and 1.8x timing factors. It discusses long-trajectory applicability, proposes GAE as future work, and explains why ProcessBench's first-error identification differs from critical-step identification.

D1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds BBEH sample sizes, trajectory-length statistics, model identification, and the 15-line grouping recipe, although the exact subset selection remains unspecified. Section 8 removes the explicit vLLM batching/caching description. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to First Return, Entropy-Eliciting Explore, BBEH, and ProcessBench, and removes the PagedAttention/vLLM reference. The ProcessBench comparison modestly refines research positioning; the broader relationship to prior work is retained.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and punctuation edits, adds an explanatory advantage footnote, expands and renames Section 8, and places the checklist before the appendices. The main narrative and section organization otherwise remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 4 and relocates Figure 3 from page 8 to page 9, with accompanying table and appendix reflow. All three existing figure graphics are unchanged, and Tables 1–3 retain their structures.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides limited empirical support for handling long reasoning trajectories and a clearer account of computational tradeoffs (Section 8 and Appendix E.5). These improve practical understanding, but the gains are modest: the BBEH subset is underspecified, grouping lacks an isolated control, and the earlier vLLM implementation explanation is removed.
